action: Scanned release/package texture roles, traced the fin-wedge use path and compared its current normal-map treatment with a no-normal proxy.
observation: Hull and Mechanical use their color payload as a normal map. The proxy improved legibility, but removing normals also changed loader fallback roughness/metalness, so that image is not a valid normal-only comparison.
decision: Do not publish the no-normal proxy; preserve material policy in a neutral-normal candidate and compare again.
next: Capture a matched baseline and corrected candidate with all target parts rendered.
evidenceScope: Static payload-role inspection plus isolated preview; the visual A/B changed material policy and is not an acceptance result.
performance: A false large normal image is a texture cost candidate; no frame-time benefit measured.

action: Compared a neutral-normal runtime proxy against the original while checking material factors and rendered target counts.
observation: The proxy preserves reported roughness and metalness and the chase image is more legible. The fitted baseline drew only four target meshes versus six for the candidate, so that close comparison is invalid; PNG-backed binding presence remains to be confirmed.
decision: Hold the candidate and avoid publishing from this incomplete comparison.
next: Repeat a warmed baseline and candidate with matching draw and binding evidence, then verify the actual package if accepted.
evidenceScope: Isolated preview only; fitted A/B incomplete and not an ordinary gameplay pass.
performance: No live frame-time or memory result.

variantCoverage.note: Fitted baseline was incomplete and binding evidence was insufficient; not an accepted A/B.

action: Inspected the shipped package's color and normal payloads and explored whether its six material-split primitives could use the existing flightStaticV3 compiler path.
observation: The color and normal slots hold separate 1,170,738-byte KTX2 images with identical compressed mip payloads. Six opaque primitives use three material hashes. A scratch build stopped first because its pilot manifest lacked required rows; source inspection separately shows flightStaticV3 is restricted to kind=place, so it cannot be enabled for this part as-is.
decision: Do not claim or publish a primitive merge, and do not bypass the compiler guards. The false-normal correction remains a candidate.
next: Review the queued correctly isolated before/candidate renderer comparison, then decide whether a supported source and package correction is justified.
evidenceScope: Package payload inspection and compiler contract trace; scratch build did not reach the merge, and renderer comparison is pending.
performance: Duplicated encoded payload is concrete; no draw-call reduction, GPU memory saving or live frame-time improvement is established.

action: Ran the source-data comparison between the shipped fin source and the prepared neutral-normal candidate.
observation: All six meshes retained positions, normals, UVs, indices and node transforms; tested base-color and metallic-roughness pixels, factors, clearcoat and emission matched. This establishes source-data preservation only; the correctly isolated renderer comparison is still queued.
decision: Keep the prepared candidate pending the actual visual and runtime-package decision.
next: Review the paired player-camera captures and validate the real loader/package if the candidate is accepted.
evidenceScope: Local source-data comparison; not an in-game visual result or published asset.
performance: No live performance measurement.

action: Inspected the current package geometry metadata and compared its named light strip with the existing isolated image.
observation: Wedge_Edge_Light accounts for 480 triangles and 490 vertices of the current package's 1,058 total triangles. The package has no authored LODs. The previous 1,566-triangle authoring note is stale for the live package; the existing image alone does not establish safe simplification.
decision: Treat the light strip as a candidate for a targeted Astra geometry/LOD comparison, not as an implemented optimization or proven frame-time problem.
next: Complete the pending baseline/candidate visual comparison first, then assess any proposed simplification against the actual player view and package contract.
evidenceScope: Current package geometry metadata plus an isolated prior candidate image; no accepted normal-map or geometry change.
performance: Triangle share is a resource count, not a measured GPU cost or frame-time benefit.

variantCoverage.note: No authored LODs in this package; runtime rendering cost is unmeasured.

action: Inspected the fin's authored trim sheet and unbound Hull ambient-occlusion image alongside the current package material slots.
observation: The trim sheet already contains panel, vent and fastener detail, so the dark rendered baseline does not establish a lack of albedo detail. The unbound Hull AO image is largely black outside sparse UV islands and is not safe to assume suitable as a generic runtime AO map.
decision: Preserve the existing trim artwork and do not blindly bind the AO image; continue the material-policy comparison.
next: Review the pending isolated material comparison through the current renderer.
evidenceScope: Source-image and package-slot inspection; no change or new player-rendered capture.
performance: No new texture sampling or live performance result.

action: Traced fin selection and the authored material tint path for player and faction palettes.
observation: The modular ship's deterministic fin selection includes fin_wedge. The authored tint function applies role-dependent color handling while retaining the texture maps. Readability of specific faction or player colors on this dark fin is not established by source inspection.
decision: Do not create additional color-variant assets based only on the code trace.
next: Compare actual composed ships with representative player and faction colors before deciding whether a palette-specific adjustment is needed.
evidenceScope: Static selection and tint trace; no composed-ship visual comparison.

action: Compared the prepared candidate's flat normal/ORM placeholder pixels and generated exact one-pixel replacements in scratch.
observation: Every original placeholder texel matched its replacement pixel: neutral normal [128,128,255,255] and ORM [255,255,255,255]. The source texture-role validator passed. The candidate has not been KTX2-encoded or rendered and the canonical asset remains unchanged.
decision: Treat the smaller placeholders as a candidate, not a shipped or GPU-validated saving.
next: If the material correction wins its visual comparison, encode and verify the actual package and assess its runtime texture behavior.
evidenceScope: Scratch source-image pixel comparison and source-role validation only.
performance: One-pixel placeholders may reduce residency relative to the candidate's 1024-square flat images; no compressed-format, GPU or frame-time result.

action: Encoded the candidate's uniform normal placeholder at 1024 and 1 pixel with the production UASTC KTX2 encoder.
observation: The 1024-square image encoded to 824 bytes with 11 mip levels; the one-pixel image encoded to 209 bytes with a complete single-level chain. Device support, renderer appearance and the final release package remain unverified.
decision: Retain the one-pixel option as a candidate pending actual runtime validation.
next: If the visual correction is accepted, encode and load the final package through its ordinary route and check the target devices.
evidenceScope: Local production-encoder output for scratch candidates; no GPU upload or player-rendered result.
performance: Encoded bytes decrease by 615 for this normal placeholder; fixed-block GPU residency should be smaller, but no measured residency or frame-time result.

action: Compared the warmed baseline, neutral-1024 and neutral-1px fin proxies in one current-renderer session, then checked material policy and capture hashes.
observation: Each shot reports six target draws. Both neutral candidates visibly reveal the existing vent and panel detail compared with the very dark baseline; their captured PNG files have identical SHA-256 in this one view. The static material-profile check reports matching coverage, fallback, roughness and metalness for baseline and 1024 candidate. The renderer's texture dimension report is incomplete for the candidates because it only checks texture.image; it cannot alone establish slot presence.
decision: Treat the neutral candidate as a promising visual correction and the 1px default as equivalent in this isolated view, while holding publication until the actual compiled package, loader, assembled palette and ordinary gameplay are verified.
next: Complete a narrow canonical source/package update through the owning Astra and compiler workers, then verify its loader and assembled player-facing result.
evidenceScope: One warm isolated renderer angle with ignored source GLB proxies plus a static application of the material-profile function; not compiled-package or ordinary-gameplay acceptance.
performance: All three frames reported six target draws; neutral KTX2 encodings were 824 versus 209 bytes, with no live GPU allocation or frame-time measurement.

action: Traced the fin's deterministic deployment against all roster ship definitions and two separately spawned non-roster craft.
observation: The 15 roster definitions resolve complete bodies rather than a modular fin in the sampled plans. The same plan chooses fin_wedge for some entity IDs of Vael writ tenders and Lamplighter wayfarers; that static selection is not a measured encounter frequency or proof of completed live admission.
decision: Review the released part through the real package loader, and target an actual modular non-roster encounter for player-facing assessment rather than attributing it to the roster starter ship.
next: Inspect the packaged renderer result and locate a representative ordinary encounter with the selected part.
evidenceScope: Production selection code and local plan evaluation; no ordinary gameplay capture.
performance: No FPS or loading improvement measured by this route trace.

action: Built the fin through the release and render-package compilers, reviewed the packaged material through the real loader, then replaced a one-pixel compressed placeholder with a four-pixel block and repeated that direct load.
observation: The first packaged candidate revealed the intended detail but emitted a compressed-texture dimension warning. The block-aligned rebuild loads without warnings in the isolated probe, reports a shared 4x4 neutral normal and draws all six meshes in both inspected views. The source geometry and authored base/roughness data remain unchanged from the original.
decision: Keep the block-aligned material correction and its scoped compiler policy. The part still needs a composed ordinary encounter and additional model iterations.
next: Inspect the pending roughness-shader comparison and seek a representative modular craft encounter.
evidenceScope: Current compiled-package loader and isolated renderer views plus source-data and focused compiler checks; no ordinary gameplay capture.
performance: The render GLB decreased from 3,706,328 to 2,535,648 bytes; each observed isolated view still submits six draws. No live frame-time or GPU-residency improvement is measured.

action: Measured the fin's existing roughness image and compared its packaged material with the extra procedural roughness shader expression removed in a browser-only diagnostic.
observation: The authored roughness channel varies across the image; the renderer confirmed four diagnostic shader rewrites. Both views submitted six meshes and showed no obvious difference at the inspected scale. This isolated experiment did not measure GPU or frame-time cost and does not establish that changing one asset's program family would improve the game.
decision: Do not ship a fin-specific shader branch without a useful matched performance result; retain the current material policy.
next: Review the fin's geometry, assembled color treatment and ordinary encounter, and revisit the shader only if a representative measurement justifies it.
evidenceScope: Source-image statistics and same-session isolated packaged-renderer comparison with a temporary browser-side shader edit; not gameplay performance or visual acceptance.
performance: No extra shader branch was shipped; no live GPU or FPS comparison was collected.

action: Priced the fin's procedural roughness expression with a same-session baseline, temporary shader removal, and restored baseline in the existing renderer cost harness.
observation: The 40-frame hard-flush scene medians were 2.680 ms, 3.525 ms and 3.715 ms respectively. The restored baseline drifted substantially from the first baseline, so this run cannot distinguish a small improvement from timing noise; it is not gameplay frame pacing.
decision: Keep the shared shader policy unchanged: this measurement does not justify an asset-specific program variant.
next: Continue the fin's assembled appearance and geometry review instead of claiming an unmeasured shader speedup.
evidenceScope: Same-session isolated renderer cost harness with a temporary diagnostic shader edit; not an ordinary-play frame-time comparison.
performance: No reliable gain demonstrated; the hard-flush medians include the isolated scene and are not live FPS.

action: Reproduced the synthetic interceptor+wedge actor with complete submission, traced hull mount and fin normalization, and checked real Vael writ-tender selection.
observation: Close/side/top reproduce the detached-looking wing at 71 draws. Identity hull mount rotations place the same positive-Z fin inward on one side and outward on the other. Actual world bounds and source LOD0 distances confirm an additional narrow-root gap. Vael writ-tender spawn data can select this pair for ordinary positive entity IDs.
decision: Treat this as an attachment/handedness defect reachable by selector, not an instance omission or observed ordinary encounter. Do not globally mirror centered fin variants.

observation: The narrowed 28-triangle bar closely retains the original light-line weight at place/close/side. The fin body finish is unchanged; all 12 comparison frames submit six draws, with no loader/texture errors. Source-to-release replaced-mesh world positions match exactly.
decision: Retain edge8thin as the light-only candidate; reject the heavier alternatives. Do not claim a frame-time gain from the triangle reduction.

action: Added a short bevelled root tab to the existing body primitive, retained the narrowed light, and compared it to mirror-only geometry in the textured interceptor+fin subset.
observation: The tab provides a visible mounting foot and closes the narrow root connection in the close comparison. All eight final assembled views submit 21 draws with no texture/loader errors. The final source preserves all 444 existing body triangles and original vertex attributes, node matrices/extras and texture payloads. An earlier Blender-joined candidate re-triangulated original faces and was rejected in favor of appending only tab geometry.
